asBirthCard.p: This one doesn't come from any sign in your chart. It comes from the date you were born. Add every digit of it together, and if the total is over 22 you add those digits again, and yours landed on exactly 22. That's the number of cards in the Major Arcana, and the card it gives you is The Fool, which is numbered zero. Zero is an odd number to be handed. The Fool comes before The Magician, who is one and the first card to pick something up and use it, and before The Fool there's nothing. You get to zero by way of 22, so you've been round the whole set once before you start. The card's planet is Uranus, which rules Aquarius and has to do with sudden breaks and the change nobody saw coming. It's counted as an air card too, and a lot of people with this birth card live a fair way ahead of themselves, in plans and ideas and what might come next.

You have a low tolerance for anything that's already been decided about you. An aunt at a birthday lunch says 'well, you know what you're like', and something in you wants to prove her wrong on the spot, even if she meant it kindly. An empty weekend doesn't bother you in the slightest, and a weekend planned to the hour has you twitchy by Saturday lunch. In meetings you're the one asking why it's done this way, and you do want to know. You aren't trying to be difficult, though it's been taken that way more than once. You've probably also heard yourself say yes to something, a trip, a move, a job in another city, before your sensible side had been consulted at all. Sometimes that's been one of the best calls you ever made. Once or twice it wasn't, and you still don't entirely regret it.

Something that gets overlooked with this card is that you don't mind being bad at things. Most adults will go a long way to avoid looking like a beginner. You'll turn up to the pottery class or the first week of a new job and ask the question everyone else in the room was too embarrassed to ask, and usually half of them were wondering the same thing. You learn fast because of it, since you aren't spending any energy protecting how you look. It also makes you the friend people ring when they're thinking about changing their life. They know you won't tell them it's mad. You'll ask what they'd need in order to try it, and the Uranian side of this card means you're honestly a bit excited for them, which they can hear in your voice.

If you never quite finish something, nobody can tell you it was bad, and some people with this card get very comfortable staying at the first draft. The business that's always about to launch. The album that's nearly done, and has been for four years. The other habit is hearing care as control. Someone who loves you asks a fair question, how the rent gets paid if you leave the job, who minds the cat if you go away for three months, and what you hear is a gate shutting. There's a little dog jumping at the traveller's heels in the picture, and people have argued for about a hundred years over whether it's cheering him on or trying to warn him. You tend to assume it's cheering. It's worth checking now and then.

When something goes badly, a loss, a knockback, months of being overlooked at work, your first move is usually to change something. Anything. The hair, the furniture, a flight booked at eleven at night, a resignation drafted in your head on the drive home. Movement feels like relief, and for a day or two it is. About a week later there's often a second stage where you go vague. Texts sit unanswered, you're cheerful on the phone and hard to pin down, and you'd sooner talk about the new plan than about what happened. The people close to you find that hard, because they turned up to help and you'd already left the building. What helps is movement that doesn't cost you anything you'll want back, like long walks or a drive to the coast. And one person you let see it before you've turned it into a story.

The card's planet, Uranus, is in detriment in Leo, which means it sits opposite its own sign and works awkwardly there. Leo is the sign of the heart, of adoring someone and being adored back, and that explains a fair bit. The first months come easily. You're funny, you'll try anything, you can turn a wet Tuesday into an outing. It's later, when someone wants to make you the centre of their world, that you can go a bit twitchy, and it's easy to mistake that for wanting out. In my experience you usually don't want out. You want the relationship to keep moving. You do best with a partner who's still changing too, and with firsts that keep coming, a new city, a hobby neither of you is any good at. When the restlessness starts pointing at the person, try pointing it at the life you've built together.

You're worth the most at the very start of something. The pilot programme, the new branch, the first six months of a business when nobody knows how it's done yet and the whole thing runs on nerve. You don't need the rulebook to exist before you begin, which makes you useful in places that haven't written one. Where it gets harder is year three of the same role, the same reports for the same people. That's when you're most likely to hand in your notice, and quite often the job wasn't really the problem. Before you leave, see whether you can get something new inside it, a project, a different team, the thing nobody's volunteered for. Contract work and roles with a clear end date suit a lot of people with this card. And find yourself a colleague who likes finishing things, and be nice to them.

At twenty this card tends to look like a lot of starts. Courses changed, flats swapped, a gap year that turned into three. There isn't much to lose yet, so the falls don't hurt much, and plenty of Fool people look back on their twenties as the years they learnt the most. By the mid-thirties it usually gets awkward. Friends have settled, there may be a mortgage or children or a partner who'd like to know where you'll be in five years, and starting again suddenly costs other people something. That's where most learn to change things from inside a life instead of by leaving it. The fifties are often kind to this card. The duties loosen, you know by then what you're actually good at, and I've seen a lot of people with it make their most interesting new start somewhere in their mid-fifties.

Keep a note on your phone called 'leaps'. Any time you feel the pull to quit, book, move or sign up for something big, write it on the note with the date and don't act on it that day. Leave it one full night. In the morning, if it still looks good, go ahead and do it properly. Most of them will still look good. The few that don't were usually about something else that was bothering you, and over a few months the note tends to show you what.
